course.title: Arabic for Beginners
course.tagline: Read and speak Arabic from zero: letters, words and simple sentences.

days.title: Say marhaba and hello
days.goal: Greet people in Arabic and say goodbye.

video.title: Arabic for Beginners — Lesson 1

steps: Watch today's video and repeat every example of greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama out loud as you hear it.
Practise greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama aloud for 10 minutes, slowly first, then at normal speed.
Write down five of your own examples using greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama.
Record yourself practising greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama and listen back, fixing any mistakes you hear.
Use greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama in a real exchange today — with a friend, family member or language partner.
days.task: Say marhaba, as-salamu alaykum and ma'a as-salama out loud five times each.
days.challenge: Greet someone in Arabic today, even by message.

quiz.explain: 'Marhaba' means hello. 'As-salamu alaykum' is a warm greeting that means 'peace be upon you.'

quiz.q: How do you say goodbye in Arabic?
quiz.explain: Ma'a as-salama means goodbye.

quiz.q: How do you greet someone with peace in Arabic?
quiz.explain: As-salamu alaykum is a greeting of peace.

days.title: Say your name in Arabic
days.goal: Introduce yourself in Arabic.

video.title: Arabic for Beginners — Lesson 1

steps: Watch today's video and repeat every example of introducing yourself: Ismi... out loud as you hear it.
Practise introducing yourself: Ismi... aloud for 10 minutes, slowly first, then at normal speed.
Write down five of your own examples using introducing yourself: Ismi....
Record yourself practising introducing yourself: Ismi... and listen back, fixing any mistakes you hear.
Use introducing yourself: Ismi... in a real exchange today — with a friend, family member or language partner.
days.task: Say 'Ismi' with your name ten times.
days.challenge: Introduce yourself in Arabic to a friend.

quiz.q: How do you say 'My name is Ada' in Arabic?
quiz.explain: 'Ismi Ada' means 'My name is Ada.'
Ismi means my name is. You say Ismi Ada for My name is Ada.

quiz.q: What should you say first when you meet someone new?
quiz.explain: Say your name first: Ismi...

days.title: Ask how someone is

video.title: Arabic for Beginners — Lesson 1

steps: Watch today's video and repeat every example of asking how someone is: Kayfa haluk? Ana bikhayr out loud as you hear it.
Practise asking how someone is: Kayfa haluk? Ana bikhayr aloud for 10 minutes, slowly first, then at normal speed.
Write down five of your own examples using asking how someone is: Kayfa haluk? Ana bikhayr.
Record yourself practising asking how someone is: Kayfa haluk? Ana bikhayr and listen back, fixing any mistakes you hear.
Use asking how someone is: Kayfa haluk? Ana bikhayr in a real exchange today — with a friend, family member or language partner.
days.task: Practise the chat: 'Kayfa haluk?' 'Ana bikhayr, shukran.'
days.challenge: Have a short greeting chat in Arabic with a friend.

quiz.explain: 'Kayfa haluk?' means 'How are you?' Answer: 'Ana bikhayr, shukran' — I am fine, thank you.
Ana bikhayr means I am fine.

options: When you want to know how someone is
quiz.explain: Kayfa haluk? means How are you?

video.title: Learn Arabic for Beginners: 24 Essential Phrases in 5 Minutes | Week 1

steps: Watch today's video and repeat every example of polite words: shukran, min fadlik, asif out loud as you hear it.
Practise polite words: shukran, min fadlik, asif aloud for 10 minutes, slowly first, then at normal speed.

days.task: Use shukran, min fadlik and asif in three practice sentences.
days.challenge: Say shukran in Arabic to someone real today.

quiz.explain: 'Shukran' means thank you. 'Min fadlik' means please, 'asif' means sorry.

quiz.q: How do you say 'please' in Arabic?
quiz.explain: Min fadlik means please.

quiz.q: How do you say 'sorry' in Arabic?
quiz.explain: Asif means sorry.

Wahid means one. Thalatha means three.

quiz.explain: 'Ma'a as-salama! Shukran' means 'Goodbye! Thank you.' It is a warm way to end.

quiz.q: What should a short greeting chat include?

quiz.explain: A short greeting chat uses greetings, asking how someone is, and saying goodbye.

You said your name with Ismi
You asked Kayfa haluk?
You answered how you are

Askunu fi... means I live in... Ana min... means I am from...

Man means who. Ayna means where, mata means when, limadha means why.

quiz.q: What do you say when you order food?

capstone.title: The Arabic Speaker
capstone.brief: Hold a five-minute chat in Arabic with a friend or teacher. Greet them, talk about your day, your family and your plans, ask them questions, and say goodbye politely. Record it.
checks: You greeted the person in Arabic
You talked about your day in Arabic
You talked about your family in Arabic
You talked about your plans in Arabic
You asked the other person at least three questions
You spoke Arabic for five minutes
You listened back and wrote down two things to improve
deliverables: A five-minute audio or video recording of your Arabic chat
A written list of 50 Arabic words you know now
A short story you wrote in Arabic (100 words or more)
A list of your three most common mistakes and how you fixed them
